subject: gk
question: Under the LERMS system, what percentage of foreign exchange earnings can be converted at the official rate?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**40%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Liberalised Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS)** was introduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **1992** as part of India's economic reforms.
 
• Under LERMS, **40% of foreign exchange earnings** were required to be converted at the **official exchange rate**, while the remaining **60% could be converted at market-determined rates.**
 
• This dual exchange rate system was implemented to address the **foreign exchange shortage** India faced in the early 1990s.
 
• The system aimed to **increase foreign exchange inflows**, reduce the **balance of payments crisis**, and bring more flexibility to the exchange rate policy.
 
• LERMS was a transitional measure that eventually led to the full **convertibility of the Indian rupee** on the current account.
 
• It marked a significant step in India's shift toward a **market-oriented economy** and liberalisation of its trade and financial systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Impact of LERMS:**

 
 
• LERMS helped improve India's **foreign exchange reserves** by encouraging exporters to bring in more foreign exchange earnings.
 
• It created a more **competitive environment** for Indian exporters as they could access market-determined exchange rates for a portion of their earnings.
 
• The system provided a **gradual transition** toward a unified exchange rate system, which was adopted in 1993.
 
 
 
• **Background of Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• India faced a **severe balance of payments crisis** in 1991, with foreign exchange reserves barely sufficient to cover a few weeks of imports.
 
• The economic reforms initiated in 1991 included measures such as **trade liberalisation**, industrial policy reforms, and fiscal consolidation, along with LERMS.
